title: Choose Codizzz's replacement visual world
question: Choose the world that should turn a client need into a visibly custom-built digital product.

options.label: Digital Pattern Room
options.lineage: industrial pattern cutting, fabrication jigs, and plotted build sheets
options.thesis: Every client need becomes a bespoke digital pattern, measured and assembled in public.
options.viewport: A requirement strip enters from the left and expands into an oversized plotted product pattern with a clear Start a build action at the registration point.
options.risk: The fabrication metaphor must remain plain enough for non-technical clients.

raised.raise: Every section gets a strict address and scan order.
Dependencies remain visibly connected instead of becoming decorative cards.
Attention is concentrated around the active requirement, never scattered.
Each state answers immediately with decisive feedback.

options.label: Decision Atlas
options.lineage: survey maps, field notebooks, and systems cartography
options.thesis: The site maps the shortest credible path from a messy need to a shipped product.
options.viewport: One dominant route crosses the fold from problem to working product, with services as precise waypoints and the consultation CTA at origin.
options.risk: Mapping is familiar in strategy work and needs sharp product demonstrations to stay proprietary.

options.label: Need Axis Specimen
options.thesis: Client priorities become live axes that visibly reshape the proposed digital product.
options.viewport: A giant CODIZZZ wordform and solution silhouette respond to Need, Scale, and Autonomy axes beside a direct project CTA.
options.case: Product clarity is excellent and the live-axis mechanism feels custom; audience identification is slightly more design-literate than the assigned world.
options.risk: The typography must demonstrate the offer rather than become a designer-only toy.

options.label: Registered Build
options.thesis: A complete product appears one registered capability layer at a time.
options.viewport: The black requirement keyline lands first; AI, AI Automation, software, web, and mobile layers register into one finished product scene.
options.case: The layered build mechanism is memorable and honest; the historical form needs careful translation for broad business clarity.
options.risk: A literal art-history treatment could overpower the digital-product proposition.

options.label: Teletext Service
options.thesis: Services become directly addressable numbered pages.
options.viewport: A 40-column service index with direct three-digit project routes.
options.case: The strict information system is useful, but its broadcast nostalgia weakens broad client identification.
options.kept: A strict address and scan order for every section.
options.risk: Retro novelty can obscure the premium custom-build proposition.

options.label: Tension Network
options.thesis: Every product is shown as a balanced network of business needs and technical forces.
options.viewport: A force diagram assembles into a digital product around the headline.
options.case: The mechanism is truthful but demands too much explanation for first-visit product clarity.
options.risk: It can read as engineering consultancy rather than digital product studio.

options.label: Luminous Understory
options.thesis: Client attention illuminates the next useful product path.
options.viewport: A glowing path discovers services by proximity.
options.case: Memorable atmosphere, but it loses both business identification and immediate offer clarity.
options.kept: One active requirement owns the page's brightest focus.
options.risk: The world can become entertainment instead of persuasion.

options.label: Workhorse Terminal
options.thesis: A client keys a need and receives an operational build response.
options.viewport: A typed requirement receives a line-by-line build plan.
options.case: Technical audiences may enjoy it, but the dark sci-fi AI trope is already overused and narrows trust.
options.kept: Every interaction answers with an unmistakable state.
options.risk: It looks like an AI demo rather than a durable product partner.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished dark AI agency page with a conventional hero, service grid, proof band, and contact CTA.
canonCard.viewport: Headline, two CTAs, abstract AI visual, trust row, and a familiar service-card fold.
canonCard.risk: Clear and professional, but deliberately indistinguishable from well-made competitors.
